_readme: Gauge provenance: the human audit trail behind aliases.json.
Each entry under `gauges` is keyed `source:site` (lookupGauge's gaugeKey) and
records that the owner personally verified this station is the correct,
commonly used gauge for the run(s) that reference it. The machine can prove a
gauge is alive and fresh (src/canarySweep.ts); only a paddler can prove it is
the RIGHT gauge. test/provenance.test.ts enforces coverage via an inverted
ratchet: lower MAX_UNAUDITED there as entries are added; 0 = fully enforcing.
`rituals` records the seasonal real-device tests: a real InReach round trip
pre-season and mid-season, the only check that exercises the Garmin POST.

usgs:12359800.notes: SF Flathead ab Twin Creek — the free-flowing wilderness reach (Youngs Creek/Bob Marshall multiday + Meadow Creek Gorge). AW quotes this gauge for both sections. NOT 12362500 (Columbia Falls), which is Hungry Horse dam outflow on a different reach. Live-verified 5,340 cfs / 8.63 ft at add time.

envdata:Wairaurahiri at Lake Hauroko.notes: Owen supplied the exact envdata.es.govt.nz share link for this run. Live-verified 45.0 m3/sec at add time via the site's own services/data.ashx JSON endpoint (reverse-engineered from base.js — no public API docs). Site is identified by exact name string, no numeric code.

flowrate:61.notes: Owen corrected this: the physical gauge sits on the Haast mainstem (flowrate.co.nz labels it 'Haast River — Roaring Billy'), a few km below the Haast/Landsborough confluence, but the run paddlers actually use it for is the Landsborough R — per packraftingtrips.nz/landsborough, published bands at Roaring Billy are 50-85 cumecs very low, 85-100 low/good, 100-150 moderate (our low/high), 150-250 high/experts only. Live-verified 93.5 m3/sec at add time via flowrate.co.nz/station/61/json/flow/current; page confirms units as Cumecs (m3/s).

usgs:09402500.notes: Owen asked for a second, mid-canyon Colorado R gauge (Lees Ferry alone is up to a day+ ahead of what's actually flowing past a party already in the canyon, since Glen Canyon Dam releases take time to propagate downstream). USGS 09402500 'COLORADO RIVER NEAR GRAND CANYON, AZ' sits at Phantom Ranch (RM ~87.5, coords 36.101,-112.086 match the Phantom Ranch/Bright Angel Creek confluence area). Same run as 'grand canyon'/'lees ferry' (AW #114, Lee's Ferry to Lake Mead) — this is a second real-time reference point on it, not a distinct trip. Live-verified 8,470 cfs / 6.67 ft at add time.
